newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Sept 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Sept 4.

text.p: -- HONG KONG ECONOMIC JOURNAL - The United States launched a missile attack on southern Iraq but the reaction of financial markets was mild. Oil prices reached the highest point since April.

-- Each candidate for chief executive of the post-1997 Hong Kong Special Aministrative Region would have to be nominated by at least 100 members of the 400-strong Selection Committee, according to a document prepared by Beijing's handpicked Preparatory Committee. This meant no more than three candidates would likely be able to stand for the position.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST - Hong Kong's top judge, Sir Ti Liang Yang, announced he would stand down to contest the position of future chief executive of Hong Kong.

-- MING PAO DAILY NEWS - China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping donated 10,000 yuan to the flood-damaged Shexian county in Hebei province. Deng had an office in the county as a branch leader of the People's Liberation Army during World War Two.

-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES - Lu Ping, China's most senior official on Hong Kong affairs, said he looked forward to shaking hands with colonial Governor Chris Patten at next year's handover ceremony marking the territory's return to China.
-- HONG KONG STANDARD - The territory's Securities & Futures Commission had argued for additional powers to impose fines on erring fund managers.
